source.title_on_document: Inspiration booster or creative fixation? The dual mechanisms of LLMs in shaping individual creativity in tasks of different complexity

supplement.where: Supplementary information at https://doi.org/10.1057/s41599-025-05867-9 (p. 10); data, survey results, conversation transcripts at https://osf.io/9ckra/ (p. 9)
supplement.holds: Supplementary Tables S1-S4 (LLM and human idea pools), Figs. S1-S4 (collaboration system), Section S5 (procedure details), Tables S5 and S6 (demographics by condition, which may give cell sizes), Tables S7 and S8 (moderated-mediation regressions). Cell-level sample sizes are not in the main text.

paper_design_summary: Two online experiments with 204 participants each, both 2 x 2 between-participants designs crossing task complexity (simple: alternative uses for a tire; complex: features and solutions for VR glasses) with the idea partner. In Experiment 1 participants were randomly assigned to read ideas from a scripted LLM partner (pre-generated ERNIE Bot ideas) or from a scripted human partner (a research assistant pasting human-written ideas); in Experiment 2 all participants had an LLM partner that sent either ten ideas per response (batch) or two ideas per response (constrained). Two blind experts rated each idea for creativity (novelty and usefulness, 1-5) and for creative fixation (similarity to the LLM ideas, 0-2), averaged per participant.

studies.label: Experiment 1 (LLM partner vs human partner, x task complexity)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Partner type (scripted LLM partner supplying ERNIE Bot ideas vs scripted human partner supplying human-written ideas), crossed with task complexity (simple vs complex)
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one condition in the two (task complexity: low vs high) by two (partner: human vs LLM) between-participants design.

arms.name: LLM partner, simple task
arms.description: Alternative uses for a tire; LLM partner posts 5 randomly selected pre-generated ERNIE Bot ideas every 100 s (6 responses, 30 ideas) over 10 min

arms.name: LLM partner, complex task
arms.description: Features and solutions for an enterprise's VR glasses; same LLM partner script

arms.name: Human partner, simple task
arms.description: Research assistant follows a script and pastes ideas from a human idea pool (ideas from eight people in the researchers' network); LLM excluded from the room

arms.name: Human partner, complex task
arms.description: Same human-partner script on the VR glasses task

participants.exclusions: None reported. The paper says 204 were recruited and randomly assigned; t-tests use df 202, ANOVAs use F(1,200), and Fig. 2 states N = 204, so all 204 appear analyzed. Cell sizes are not given in the main text (demographics by condition are in Supplementary Table S5).
participants.who: Adults recruited for monetary compensation who had experience using LLM tools; mean age 27.73; 54.9% female; 91.18% with a bachelor's degree or above. Recruitment source not stated.
participants.country: Not stated explicitly; Chinese-language context (ERNIE Bot chosen for 'the participants' linguistic background', p. 8; Renmin University ethics approval, p. 10)
participants.quote: We recruited 204 participants in return for monetary compensation, requiring them to have experience using LLM tools.

ai_tool.name_model: ERNIE Bot (Baidu); scripted: 50 ideas generated in advance, partner posts randomly selected ones
ai_tool.how_used: Participants read ideas posted in a chat by the LLM partner (5 ideas every 100 s, 30 in total) while typing their own ideas into a text box; the LLM idea pool and the human idea pool were rated equally creative (p. 4).

task.description: Simple task: alternative uses for a tire (alternative uses test). Complex task: innovative feature points and solutions for VR glasses developed by an enterprise. Generate as many ideas as possible.

outcomes.name: Objective creativity score (expert-rated)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two trained independent external experts, blind to demographics, hypotheses and design, rated each idea on overall novelty and usefulness on a 1-5 scale; ICC = 0.847; average used as each participant's overall creativity score (p. 5).

contrasts.reported: One-way ANOVA F(1,202) = 4.638, P = 0.032, partial eta^2 = 0.022; M_human = 2.311, s.d. = 0.469 vs M_LLM = 2.45, s.d. = 0.453; t(202) = -2.154; P = 0.032; d = -0.301; 95% CI (-0.266, -0.012). 2 x 2 ANOVA main effect of partner type F(1,200) = 4.901, P = 0.028, partial eta^2 = 0.024; interaction F(1,200) = 13.272, P < 0.001, partial eta^2 = 0.062. Arm ns not printed (total N = 204).
contrasts.locator: p. 5, Results, Experiment 1 (Self-reported creativity and Creativity paragraphs)

contrasts.reported: M_LLM = 2.351, s.d. = 0.62 vs M_human = 2.441, s.d. = 0.63; F(1,200) = 1.021; P = 0.028; partial eta^2 = 0.005 (as printed; F = 1.021 and P = 0.028 do not agree). Cell ns not printed. Fig. 2 plots cell means with s.e.m.
contrasts.locator: p. 5, Results, Experiment 1, Creativity; p. 6, Fig. 2

contrasts.reported: M_LLM = 2.549, s.d. = 0.62 vs M_human = 2.182, s.d. = 0.63; F(1,200) = 17.152; P < 0.001; partial eta^2 = 0.079. Cell ns not printed. Fig. 2 plots cell means with s.e.m.
contrasts.locator: p. 5, Results, Experiment 1, Creativity; p. 6, Fig. 2

outcomes.name: Creative fixation (expert-rated similarity to LLM ideas)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two experts rated each idea's overall similarity to the ideas already generated by the LLM on a 0-2 scale (0 = copies no keywords or ideas, 1 = copies a keyword or idea but expands or modifies it, 2 = nearly copies an existing one); ICC = 0.885; averaged per participant. Used as a mediator. The paper does not say what the human-partner condition's ideas were compared against.

contrasts.reported: Complex task: beta = 1.449, SE = 0.154, P < 0.001 (LLM partner increased fixation). Simple task (Fig. 3): beta = 0.013, P = 0.935. Conditional indirect effect via fixation, complex: omega_M1 = -0.322, 95% CI (-0.536, -0.120); simple: -0.003, 95% CI (-0.044, 0.045). Higher fixation is less creative work, so the sign is reversed relative to creativity.
contrasts.locator: p. 6, Moderated mediation and Fig. 3; regressions in Supplementary Table S7

outcomes.name: Self-reported creativity
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Scale item such as 'How do you rate your creative performance in this task?', 5-point scale. Not eligible (self-report); listed for completeness. The paper also reports the gap between self-reported and expert scores.

studies.label: Experiment 2 (constrained vs batch LLM responses, x task complexity)

assignment.what_was_assigned: LLM response type (batch-responsive: ten ideas per response vs constrained-responsive: two ideas per response), crossed with task complexity (simple vs complex)
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one condition in the two (task complexity: low vs high) by two (LLM response type: batch-responsive vs constrained-responsive) between-participants design.

arms.name: Constrained-responsive LLM, simple task
arms.description: LLM partner posts 2 ideas every 40 s (15 responses, 30 ideas) over 10 min; tire alternative uses

arms.name: Batch-responsive LLM, simple task
arms.description: LLM partner posts 10 ideas every 200 s (3 responses, 30 ideas) over 10 min; tire alternative uses

participants.exclusions: None reported. 204 recruited and randomly assigned; t-tests use df 202, ANOVAs F(1,200), and Fig. 4 states N = 204. Cell sizes not in the main text (Supplementary Table S6).
participants.who: Adults recruited for monetary compensation who had experience using LLM tools; mean age 29; 58.8% female; 94.12% with a bachelor's degree or above. Recruitment source not stated. The paper does not say whether these are different people from Experiment 1.
participants.quote: We recruited 204 participants in return for monetary compensation, requiring them to have experience using LLM tools.

ai_tool.name_model: ERNIE Bot (Baidu); scripted pre-generated idea pool
ai_tool.how_used: LLM partner posted pre-generated ideas in the chat at a fixed schedule; both arms received 30 ideas in total, differing only in ideas per response and interval (p. 3).

task.description: Same tasks as Experiment 1: alternative uses for a tire (simple) and features and solutions for VR glasses (complex). Generate as many ideas as possible.

outcomes.name: Objective creativity score (expert-rated)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two well-trained experts independently coded creativity with the Experiment 1 scales (novelty and usefulness, 1-5); ICC = 0.841; average used as each participant's score (p. 5).

contrasts.reported: 2 x 2 ANOVA main effect of LLM response type F(1,200) = 0.811, P = 0.369, partial eta^2 = 0.004; task complexity F(1,200) = 0.049, P = 0.826; interaction F(1,200) = 49.984, P < 0.001, partial eta^2 = 0.200.

M_batch = 2.139, s.d. = 0.048 vs M_constrained = 2.520, s.d. = 0.047; F(1,200) = 31.765; P < 0.001; partial eta^2 = 0.137. The printed s.d. values (about 0.05) look like standard errors given Fig. 4 error bars (s.e.m.); cell ns not printed.
M_batch = 2.466, s.d. = 0.048 vs M_constrained = 2.171, s.d. = 0.047; F(1,200) = 19.031; P < 0.001; partial eta^2 = 0.087. Same caveat on s.d.; cell ns not printed.

outcomes.name: Creative fixation (expert-rated similarity to LLM ideas)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two experts coded creative fixation with the Experiment 1 scale (0-2 similarity to LLM ideas); ICC = 0.900; averaged per participant. Used as a mediator.

contrasts.reported: Complex task: beta = -1.433, SE = 0.159, P < 0.001 (constraint decreased fixation). Simple task (Fig. 5): beta = -0.071, P = 0.655. Conditional indirect effect via fixation, complex: omega_M1 = 0.371, 95% CI (0.158, 0.624); simple: 0.018, 95% CI (-0.043, 0.090). Higher fixation is less creative work, so the sign is reversed relative to creativity.
contrasts.locator: p. 7, Moderated mediation and Fig. 5; regressions in Supplementary Table S8

outcomes.name: Self-reported creativity
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Self-rated creativity, 5-point scale. Not eligible (self-report); listed for completeness.

eligibility.reason: Experiment 1 randomly assigned 204 people to read ideas from an LLM partner (pre-generated ERNIE Bot ideas) or a scripted human partner while generating ideas, and experts rated each participant's ideas for creativity (p. 4-5). Experiment 2 (204 people) is an ai_design contrast (2 vs 10 ideas per LLM response). Caveats: the AI is a scripted feed of pre-generated ideas, not interactive chat; the comparison arm receives human-written ideas, so the contrast is ai_vs_active; cell sizes are only in Supplementary Tables S5-S6.

one_line_finding: Reading LLM-supplied ideas raised expert-rated creativity relative to a human partner overall (2.45 vs 2.311, d = -0.301 as printed, P = 0.032), raising it on a simple alternative-uses task (2.549 vs 2.182) and lowering it on a complex product task (2.351 vs 2.441); in Experiment 2, two ideas per LLM response beat ten on the complex task (2.520 vs 2.139) but not the simple one (2.171 vs 2.466) (pp. 5-7).
open_questions: Exp. 1 complex-task contrast prints F(1,200) = 1.021 with P = 0.028 (p. 5); these are inconsistent, and the significance of the complex-task decline is uncertain.
Exp. 2 cell 's.d.' values of 0.047-0.048 (p. 7) look like standard errors, not standard deviations; check against OSF data or the supplement before standardizing.
Cell sizes per arm are not in the main text; Supplementary Tables S5 and S6 may give them.
Whether Experiment 1 and Experiment 2 used different participants is not stated.
In the human-partner condition, it is not stated what creative fixation was measured against (the measure is defined as similarity to LLM ideas).
notes: Both experiments use the same two tasks; the simple task is an alternative-uses test (tire) and the complex task is product ideation (VR glasses), so task type is coded idea_generation for the study. Inspirational stimulation (5-item self-report, alpha = 0.968) is a mediator and is not listed as an outcome. Manipulation checks are not listed. No fluency or diversity outcome is reported in the main text. The human and LLM idea pools were rated equally creative (p. 4: M_human = 2.200 vs M_LLM = 2.160 simple; 2.180 vs 2.200 complex).
